A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Task Preference Optimization work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original TPO benchmark results, component and data ablations, and qualitative predictions in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds LLaVA-OneVision benchmark results and training-time measurements.

M1.justification: The task tokens, region/temporal/mask heads, combined training objective, and three-stage training procedure remain unchanged. Revised explanations and additional cost documentation do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: v2 adds a standalone PerceptionTest evaluation for LLaVA-OV and LLaVA-OV-TPO in appendix Table 16. VideoMME was already evaluated with VideoChat, and the training datasets remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The new training-cost comparison explicitly evaluates TPO against textualized-task training and conversation-only training (v2 Table 19). Comparator membership in the retained predictive-performance tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds a stage-wise training-time comparison on 64 GPUs, describing a same-data comparison between TPO and textualized training. Existing accuracy protocols and training settings are retained; the timing disclosure does not establish reruns or changed settings for those experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds an overhead analysis comparing task-head supervision, textualized supervision, and removal of visual-task training (Table 19). The original head, reasoning-data, co-training, and data-scaling ablations and qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 6 changes VideoChat-TPO's QVHighlight mAP from 38.8 to 38.6 and HIT@1 from 66.2 to 65.4. New Table 16 reports LLaVA-OV/TPO scores of 58.2/61.3 on VideoMME and 57.1/64.0 on PerceptionTest; Table 19 adds stage-wise runtimes. The repeated LLaVA MVBench results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (1), task-token and embedding definitions, and the mathematical formulation are unchanged. Neither version supplies additional theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal claims: improved multimodal understanding, the reported 14.6% overall improvement, multi-task synergy, scalability, and expert-comparable task performance. The additions support existing contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of training overhead and explains that auxiliary encoders incur inference cost only when their task heads are activated. It also interprets the new LLaVA results as improvements in fine-grained perception and long-video understanding. The existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix Section 2 newly documents GPU counts, per-stage training times, and auxiliary-encoder use during training and inference. Existing hyperparameters, data tables, instruction templates, and the repository link are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Fengwu and Perception Test and prunes background references including Genie, GPT-4o, and InternVideo. The central positioning relative to textualized prediction, task decoders, and preference optimization remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes sentence-level corrections and paragraph refinements, fixes the multi-image results reference from Table 14 to Table 4, and renames the first appendix section. It adds an affiliation and acknowledgements while retaining the overall narrative structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds appendix Tables 16 and 19; Table 16 redisplays existing MVBench results alongside new benchmark columns. Table 1 moves columns, and appendix text and instruction tables are reflowed and renumbered. The eight figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: The additional LLaVA evaluations modestly strengthen evidence of transfer across models, while runtime reporting and corrected cross-references improve transparency. The cost interpretation needs qualification: the claimed roughly 25% overhead matches stage 3 alone (52 versus 42 hours); summing Table 19 gives 63.5 versus 42 hours, about 51%. These are useful but limited gains with a remaining reporting ambiguity.
